title: activation-velocity-sprint-canvas-3phase
content:
Activation Velocity Sprint Canvas — 3-Phase Onramp (experimental lightweight template)

Purpose: a compact, action-first 30/60/90 onboarding canvas aimed at high-velocity customer launches where we prioritize time-to-first-valuable-call, predictable capacity needs, and an early renewal signal. Designed for CSMs running technical + adoption playbooks simultaneously.

Status: Draft — iterative. Use as a quick starting script for high-touch pilots; explicit handoff checkpoints embedded.

1) One-line objective
- Get the customer to 3 production-shaped inference workflows (pilot -> staging -> prod) within 90 days with baseline latency < target SLO and first meaningful ROI metric visible (cost-per-call reduction or user engagement uplift).

2) Primary outcome metrics (what defines success)
- Time-to-first-production-call: <= 21 days
- Latency SLO for pilot model: p95 <= 350ms for 128-token average prompt
- Token cost per inference: baseline and target (capture in sheet)
- Adoption metric: 10% of target user base using feature daily by day 90 (or equivalent product KPI)
- Renewal signal: customer commits to a Dedicated capacity evaluation by day 75 if throughput exceeds baseline thresholds

3) Baseline & starting data (fill during kickoff)
- Current infra: (edge/cloud/on-prem) — note here
- Current model(s): {model-name(s)} (versions)
- Estimated QPS for MVP flows: X
- Billing/account contacts and org security constraints (IP allowlists, SCIM, KMS)
- Key stakeholders: product owner, infra lead, security owner, procurement

4) Customer persona & priority flows
- Primary persona: Product manager delivering LLM feature, cares about latency & UX
- Secondary persona: Platform engineer (reason: peformance, cost)
- Priority flows: "autocomplete for invoices" (Flow A), "contextual answer widget" (Flow B), "search re-rank" (Flow C)

5) 3-Phase plan (high level)
- Phase A (0–14 days): Kickoff -> Integration -> First calls
  - Goals: API integration, initial model selection, instrumenting metrics, first 100 API calls
  - Deliverables: Postman/SDK integration, scoreboard doc with p50/p95, simple dashboard link
  - Quick wins: prefix caching for repeated prompts, reduce payload size

- Phase B (15–45 days): Stabilize -> Optimize -> Enable users
  - Goals: Reduce variance, enable KV caching, tune batching, first A/B test for prompt
  - Deliverables: baseline latency report, cost vs quantization options, onboarding training (1 session), runbook for common errors
  - Acceptance criteria to move to Phase C: sustained p95 within 20% of target for 3 consecutive days + <2 production incidents

- Phase C (46–90 days): Scale -> Harden -> Handoff to success ops
  - Goals: Throughput tuning (autoscale policies), fallback routing, rollout plan for production model pinning
  - Deliverables: SLA/RTO draft for customer, final handoff doc, renewal recommendation brief
  - Renewal trigger: usage meets threshold OR customer signs for Dedicated trial

6) Week-by-week micro-checklist (practical tasks, copyable)
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): account setup, invite CSM/SEs, confirm contacts, send pre-kickoff survey
- Week 1 (days 1–7): kickoff, create workspace, exchange API keys or set up VPC peering, run sample calls, capture p50/p95
- Week 2 (days 8–14): integrate into product flow, tag telemetry, identify top latency contributors, enable caching if applicable
- Week 3–4 (days 15–30): introduce quantization/variant for cost test, start controlled A/B with 10% of traffic, run user feedback session
- Week 5–6 (days 31–45): iterate prompts, finalize autoscaling policy, document runbook entries for common errors
- Week 7–13 (days 46–90): ramp traffic, execute rollout plan, finalize long-term support model, present renewal brief to customer execs

7) Technical gating checklist (CSM + SE signoff)
- Integration: sample calls succeed, logs flowing to our console
- Latency: p95 meets Phase acceptance window for 72h
- Stability: < 2 distinct error classes in logs over 7 days
- Security: KMS integration validated OR customer acknowledges risk for hosted keys; network allowlists configured
- Cost: suggested cost-optimization path documented

8) Communication templates (shortened, ready-to-send snippets)
- Kickoff invite subject: "Redwood + <Customer>: Onramp Kickoff — week of <date>"
  - Body snippet: "Quick agenda: 30m intro, integration checklist, success metrics, next steps. Please bring product and infra leads. Link to pre-kickoff survey: <sheet>"
- Progress update subject: "Week 2 update — Integration progress + blockers"
  - Body snippet: bullet list of completed items, next actions, asks for customer

9) Risk register (quick triage with mitigations)
- Risk: Customer cannot open peering / network constraints
  - Mitigation: Offer hosted API proxy or local docker dev env; escalate to infra partner
- Risk: Latency variance due to long context inputs
  - Mitigation: Implement prompt truncation guidelines + streaming where applicable
- Risk: Procurement delays for Dedicated eval
  - Mitigation: Offer timeboxed pilot with clear rollback; capture exec-level value brief

10) Hand-off & renewal artefacts (what we send at 75–90d)
- Handoff doc: architecture diagram, runbook, metrics dashboard, contact matrix, billing overview
- Renewal brief: usage summary, performance vs SLO, recommended next step (Dedicated/prod plan), ROI snapshot
- Exec slide: 1-page one-pager for customer exec with key results and ask (signature for pilot/Dedicated)

11) Quick metrics capture sheet (fields to copy into spreadsheet)
- Metric name | Baseline | Current | Target | Notes
- e.g. p50 latency | 220ms | 180ms | 160ms | after caching
- daily API calls | 0 | 350 | 3,000 | extrapolate for month 3

12) Running notes / things to iterate (notes to self)
- Consider a lightweight "pilot SLA" that is just p95 & incident escalation timeline — customers like concrete numbers
- Add a small section for procurement tickboxes (PO number, SOW needed?) next version
- Make an SDK-based quickstart for our most common flows (search & chat) and reference in Phase A

13) Open questions (needs answers before Phase B)
- Does customer require private deployment or is hosted acceptable for pilot? (ask security owner)
- Which model variants are Redwood-verified for target latency at customer region? (ask Solutions Eng)
- What’s the traffic forecast if feature is adopted by 20% of power users? (ask PM)

14) Short meeting agendas (copyable)
- Kickoff (30m): intros (5m), objectives & success metrics (5m), integration checklist (10m), next steps owner mapping (10m)
- Stabilization sync (30m): recent incidents (5m), telemetry review (10m), tuning recommendations (10m), blockers & owners (5m)

15) Quick acceptance checklist for CSM to sign (single line each)
- Customer completed API integration [ ]
- Telemetry validated in Console [ ]
- Latency & error thresholds acceptable to customer [ ]
- Training session delivered to product team [ ]
- Renewal recommendation drafted [ ]

Footer: This is an experimental canvas — please copy into customer-specific doc and fill the Baseline & Week-by-week sections before kickoff.

References / Links: Confluence onboarding canvas (link in linked_artifacts), relevant Jira ticket(s) for provisioning, example onboarding code in GitHub.

Notes: informal / working doc — shorthand allowed. Add missing stakeholders and tag with #pilot when creating a customer-specific copy.
